result_text:
I changed the mock-folder test convention so any folder starting with `mock` or `__mock` counts as test code. The full `codeanalyzer` suite passes (332 tests, 3 skipped, none failing).

**What changed**

- `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`: I replaced the two folder rules (`__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+` and `mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+`) with one rule, `(.*[/\\])?(__)?mock[^/\\]*[/\\].*`. The rest of the folder name is any characters except a path separator, so `mock`, `mock.data`, `mock(old)` and `mock-größe` all match. The name must start at a path-segment boundary, so `remock/` and `src/main/java/` do not match, and a file named `mock.java` does not match because it has no folder after it. Backslash paths work because `SourceFileFilter.pathMatches` already tries the separator variants. The existing `mockapi`, `_mock.*` file and `[Mm]ocks` rules are untouched, and `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` still match.
- `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsTest.java` (new): checks that the cases above are test scope and that `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java`, `mockery.java` and `Mock.java` are not.

I did not commit anything.
